policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'in the last days' with the note 'Greek in the last of the days' renders the phrase ep' eschaton/eschatou ton hemeron identically either way; the singular/plural form of the substantive is invisible in the English.
ASV 'mockers shall come with mockery' renders en empaigmone explicitly; the omission would leave 'with mockery' untranslated.
ASV 'by the same word' renders the intensive/identifying auto(i) (to auto logo); the genitive autou would give 'by his word', which the ASV does not print.
ASV 'The Lord' is the ordinary English rendering of kyrios with or without the Greek article; nothing in the verse or its notes distinguishes the articular from the anarthrous reading.
ASV 'is longsuffering to you-ward' renders the second-person hymas; hemas would require 'to us-ward'.
ASV 'the day of the Lord' supplies the English definite article as normal for a definite genitive construction, so it does not show whether the Greek printed the article before hemera.
ASV 'will come as a thief' has no rendering of en nykti; the longer reading would give 'as a thief in the night'.
ASV 'the elements shall be dissolved' is the same English for the singular or plural verb with the neuter plural subject stoicheia; Greek verb number is not visible in the translation.

ASV text 'the earth and the works that are therein shall be burned up' renders katakaesetai; the ASV note 'The most ancient manuscripts read discovered' explicitly relegates heurethesetai to the margin, confirming katakaesetai as the text translated.
ASV 'Seeing that these things are thus all to be dissolved' renders houtos with 'thus'; the inferential oun would give 'therefore' and leave 'thus' unaccounted for.

ASV 'according to the wisdom given to him' fixes the English order regardless of whether the Greek printed dotheisan auto or auto dotheisan; this is a word-order variant with no effect on the rendering.
ASV 'in all his epistles' supplies a possessive rather than an article, and English requires a determiner here either way, so the presence or absence of tais is not distinguished.
ASV 'wherein are some things hard to be understood' is equally ambiguous as to antecedent: the feminine hais (the epistles) and the masculine/neuter hois (the things spoken of) both yield 'wherein'.
ASV prints 'Amen.' at the close of the verse, rendering amen; the omission would end at 'both now and for ever'.
